title: Compute-Matched Repetition Advantage in Long-CoT Supervised Fine-Tuning

contributions.purpose: Enable a fair, compute-controlled comparison between repeating a small curated dataset and scaling to more unique data in long-CoT SFT, removing the token-count confound.
contributions.mechanism: Token-budget matching: early-stop the repetition condition when its cumulative response tokens reach the data-scaling baseline's total token budget, rather than matching optimizer steps.
contributions.evaluation: Achieves 0.50% token deviation and 0.56% FLOPs deviation between conditions.
contributions.source_quote: We propose token-budget matching as a methodology for fair compute-controlled comparisons in long-CoT SFT, achieving 0.50% token deviation and 0.56% FLOPs deviation between conditions.

contributions.purpose: Test whether the reported repetition advantage is genuine or merely an artifact of the compute (token) disparity in prior step-matched comparisons.
contributions.mechanism: Compare repetition vs data-scaling under token-matched conditions and compute a delta-tok/delta-step ratio against a refutation threshold.
contributions.evaluation: Repetition advantage is not a compute artifact: under token-matched conditions it is preserved and amplified with a 6.33x (delta-tok/delta-step) ratio on aggregate Pass@k, far exceeding the 0.8 threshold for refuting the compute confound.
contributions.domain: Data-repetition vs data-scaling for reasoning SFT
contributions.source_quote: We demonstrate that the repetition advantage is not a compute artifact: under token-matched conditions, the advantage is preserved and amplified 6.33x (delta-tok/delta-step) ratio on aggregate Pass@k, far exceeding the 0.8 threshold for refuting the compute confound.

contributions.purpose: Explain the mechanism by which repetition training improves long-CoT performance.
contributions.mechanism: Analyze termination rates and conditional accuracy of models trained with repetition vs data scaling.
contributions.evaluation: Repetition-trained models achieve dramatically higher termination rates (87-91% vs 29-48%) rather than better conditional accuracy, learning to produce complete, decisive reasoning chains.
contributions.domain: Mechanistic analysis of the repetition advantage
contributions.source_quote: We identify the mechanism underlying the repetition advantage: models trained with repetition achieve dramatically higher termination rates (87-91% vs 29-48%), learning to produce complete, decisive reasoning chains rather than better individual answers.

self_declared_provenance.quote: A surprising finding from Kopiczko et al. (2026) challenges conventional wisdom about data scaling in long-CoT SFT: training on 1,600 carefully curated samples repeated 32 times outperforms training on 51,200 unique samples for the same number of optimizer steps. This 'repetition advantage'...

Most recently, Kopiczko et al. (2026) show that in long-CoT SFT, repeating a small curated dataset for multiple epochs outperforms training on 32x more unique data under step-matched conditions. However, their step-matched comparison gives the repetition condition approximately 3% more training tokens due to longer response sequences... Our work addresses this gap by introducing token-budget matching, which controls for total training tokens rather than steps, providing the first rigorous isolation of the repetition effect in long-CoT SFT.

Muennighoff et al. (2023) investigate scaling laws under data-constrained regimes... However, these studies focus on pretraining rather than supervised fine-tuning, where the dynamics of repetition may differ substantially due to the smaller dataset sizes and task-specific nature of the training signal.

notes: Positive/confirmatory result: rigorously reaffirms and strengthens Kopiczko et al. (2026)'s repetition advantage after removing the compute confound. No negative or tie result.
